answer: Charge every agent a fee to mint an identity, then refund it only if that identity survives a full epoch of real work. A comet crossing the sky costs nothing to watch but a great deal to launch, and a sybil farmer pays that launch cost hundreds of times before any clone earns a vote. Pair it with an atlas of observed behavior: the network maps which identities transact together, and clusters sharing timing, fee patterns, or counterparties collapse into one node. An honest meadow of scattered agents never looks like a fleet.
